guard_streams.source: Refresher messaging on Silent and Abandoned Calls
guard_streams.write_limit: Call-misuse rules and enforcement penalties are communications-compliance evidence, not broadband availability or measured speed.

facts.detail: Ofcom published the refresher on 22 January 2026.
Silent and abandoned calls are described as misuse of electronic communications services and networks.
Organisations should design automated calling, dialler and call-handling systems to prevent these calls.
Repeated silent or abandoned calls may amount to persistent misuse under the Communications Act 2003.
Persistent misuse may result in a financial penalty of up to £2 million.
Liability can apply to any person or organisation, including call centres and communications providers.
Communications providers are reminded of General Condition B1 duties concerning efficient and effective number use.
Non-compliance with relevant number-use conditions can lead to penalties of up to 10% of turnover.
Ofcom operated an enforcement programme concerning this misuse between 2006 and 2023.
The guidance distinguishes silent calls with no caller present from abandoned calls where a live-agent call is dropped or replaced by a message.

guard_streams.source: Signal struggles on trains widespread, Ofcom research finds
guard_streams.write_limit: Mobile measurements on railway segments and train Wi-Fi results cannot be transferred to fixed-broadband parcels.

facts.detail: Ofcom published the train-connectivity findings on 3 June 2026.
Mobile performance was poor on between 58% and 83% of train tests depending on network.
The study measured 24 segments of key railway lines.
The measured railway segments covered England, Scotland and Wales.
Good performance required at least 5 Mbit/s download, 1.5 Mbit/s upload and response time no more than 50 ms.
EE met the good-performance standard on 42% of measured railway segments.
Three met the standard on 21%, O2 on 20% and Vodafone on 17% of measured segments.
Train-company onboard Wi-Fi performed well only 1% of the time.
The source identifies weak ground-mast signal around rail lines and difficult-to-penetrate carriage types as core factors.
Railway mobile measurements are kept separate from fixed-line parcel coverage.
